documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 y/o retired construction worker transferring care; brought a bag of bottles.

HPI: Long-standing high blood pressure and what his last doctor called heart failure, diagnosed a few years back after he got winded and puffy; he thinks he had an ultrasound of the heart then. Weighs himself 'when I remember.' No orthopnea or PND now, walks the block without stopping, ankles fine. Knees ache on stairs and after yard work, both sides, for years; doesn't take anything for it. Treated for TB about 18 years ago, finished the pills, no problems since. Had pneumonia this past February, treated with antibiotics at the old office, felt back to normal within a few weeks.

Meds (verified from bottles): lisinopril 20 daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, HCTZ 25 daily, furosemide 40 qAM, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily.
Allergies: none to drugs.
PSH: none.
FHx: father MI at 62. Mother HTN and type 2 DM. Brother high cholesterol.
Social: divorced, lives alone, daughter nearby and checks on him. Smoked about a pack a day for 40 years, quit in 2012. 1-2 beers a week. Retired from construction.

Exam: well appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. JVP not elevated. No peripheral edema. Knees with crepitus, no effusion, full ROM. Skin: weathered, sun-damaged face and forearms.

A/P:
1. HTN - at goal today on current regimen. BMP.
2. Chronic heart failure, sounds like preserved EF - asked for the echo with old records. Euvolemic. Daily weights reviewed.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorva 40 - lipids today.
4. Knee OA - activity as tolerated.
5. Remote treated TB, recent pneumonia - records requested.
6. HM: HCV/HIV once today. Colonoscopy he thinks 2017, will confirm. Lung cancer screening eligible (40 pk-yr, quit 8 yrs ago) - discuss next visit. Flu shot at nurse visit next month.
RTC ~4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Talbot, your bloodwork from yesterday looks good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on your water pills, blood counts are normal, and your cholesterol is in a reasonable range on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes. See you in January.

reports.text: Outside study, prior office. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. LVEF estimated 55%. Impaired LV relaxation pattern on mitral inflow. Right ventricle normal size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Preserved LV systolic function, LVEF 55%. Impaired relaxation. No significant valve disease.

reports.text: Outside study, prior office. Follow-up after pneumonia. Lungs clear. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size within normal limits.
reports.conclusion: Clear lungs.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 38 pages received by fax from prior PCP office. Includes: problem list (HTN, heart failure, high cholesterol, knee arthritis, history of TB), med list matching ours, 2019 echocardiogram (EF 55%, impaired relaxation), February 2020 office notes for pneumonia treated with oral antibiotics, March 2020 follow-up chest x-ray clear, 2017 colonoscopy report (normal, repeat 10 years), Tdap 2017. Scanned. Flagged for PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old records reviewed. Echo 2019 EF 55% with impaired relaxation - fits HFpEF, problem list updated. Pneumonia Feb 2020 resolved, CXR clear 3/2020. Colonoscopy 2017 normal, next 2027. Tdap 2017.

medications.sig: Apply thin layer to left cheek twice daily for 3 weeks

reports.text: Specimen: skin, left cheek, shave biopsy. Microscopic: hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis overlying atypical basal keratinocytes confined to the lower epidermis, with solar elastosis in the dermis. No full-thickness atypia. No invasive carcinoma. Margins: peripheral margin involved by actinic change.
reports.conclusion: Hypertrophic actinic keratosis. No squamous cell carcinoma identified.

procedures.procedure: Shave biopsy of lesion of skin of head or neck
Cryotherapy of skin lesion with liquid nitrogen

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group. Date of visit: 05/31/2022. Received by fax 06/21/2022.

Thank you for sending Mr. Talbot, 66, retired construction worker with long outdoor exposure and little sunscreen use.
Concern: left cheek patch growing slowly over the past year; itchy at times, mostly no symptoms.
Meds per patient: lisinopril, metoprolol, furosemide, atorvastatin, aspirin. Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker.
Exam: Left malar cheek, sun-exposed, 1.5 cm erythematous scaly plaque with a slightly elevated, irregular border. Several smaller scaly lesions of similar character on the scalp and dorsal hands. No cervical or preauricular lymphadenopathy.
Procedure: shave biopsy left cheek plaque. Liquid nitrogen cryotherapy to 6 lesions of scalp and dorsal hands.
Pathology (06/03): hypertrophic actinic keratosis, no carcinoma.
Assessment: actinic keratoses, cheek lesion hypertrophic.
Plan: 5-fluorouracil 5% cream to the left cheek twice daily for 3 weeks; expect redness and crusting. Broad-spectrum SPF daily, hat outdoors. Skin check in 12 months.

documents.title: Skin cream question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling for a refill of metoprolol and mentioned the skin doctor gave him a cream for his cheek that's making it red and crusty after a week. Told him the dermatologist expects that with this cream and to call their office if it's raw or bleeding. Metoprolol tartrate refill sent, 90 days.

documents.title: Dermatology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm letter arrived 3 wks after his visit. Biopsy AK without cancer, cryo to scalp/hands, 5-FU course. Added AK to list. He'd already told us about the cream at a refill call.

documents.title: Call from daughter
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter (on HIPAA form) calling. Worried her father has pulled back from people over the summer - skipped the family cookout, doesn't call friends. She thinks it's his hearing: he doesn't answer when she calls him from the next room and the TV is blasting. He gets annoyed when he can't follow conversation. No safety concerns, eating fine. Offered visit next week, she'll bring him. Booked 9/8.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - hearing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter.
She notes he doesn't respond when she calls from another room and keeps the TV much louder than he used to. He admits he's frustrated - can't follow what people are saying, especially in restaurants or at family gatherings, so he's been staying home. No ear pain, no drainage, no spinning. No new meds.
PHQ-9 4: low mood is about the hearing, sleeping and eating fine, no SI.
Exam: canals clear both sides, TMs intact and normal. Conversational voice fine face to face, misses words when I turn away.
A/P: Bilateral hearing loss, likely age-related given years of job-site noise. ENT/audiology referral. Mood: situational, will recheck once hearing is addressed.
BP a little up today, he was keyed up about this visit - recheck next time. HF stable.

reports.text: Pure-tone audiometry: bilateral symmetric sensorineural hearing loss, mild in the low frequencies sloping to moderate in the high frequencies. Air-bone gaps absent. Speech reception thresholds consistent with pure tones. Word recognition good bilaterally. Tympanometry type A both ears.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral symmetric sensorineural hearing loss, mild sloping to moderate. Candidate for amplification.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside ENT practice. Date of service 10/05/2022. Received 12/13/2022.

Reason for referral: hearing.
History: 67-year-old man, history of hypertension, heart failure, hyperlipidemia, arthritis and treated TB. His daughter reports he often does not respond when called from another room and turns the television up well beyond his old level. He is frustrated by trouble following conversation in noisy settings and has been avoiding social events. Denies otalgia, otorrhea and vertigo.
Medications: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81. NKDA.
Exam: otoscopy normal bilaterally. Whispered voice test: reduced recognition of whispered phrases on both sides. Rinne and Weber without lateralizing or conductive pattern. Head and neck exam otherwise normal.
Audiology: see attached audiogram, symmetric SNHL mild sloping to moderate, good word recognition.
Impression: presbycusis.
Plan: bilateral hearing aids, referred to our audiologist for fitting. Communication strategies reviewed with patient and daughter. Return as needed.

documents.title: Fall vaccines

documents.title: Hearing aids

documents.title: RE: Hearing aids
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great to hear. Thanks for letting us know - we haven't received the ENT notes yet but will watch for them.

documents.title: ENT records reviewed
documents.author: PCP

orders.reason: painless gross hematuria, 40 pack-year former smoker

documents.title: Office Visit - hematuria
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 3 weeks of intermittent pink urine, mostly mornings. No pain, no burning, no urgency or frequency, no flank pain, no fever. No injury. On aspirin 81 only.
Exam: comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness.
UA: blood positive, 25 RBC/hpf, no WBC, LE and nitrite negative. Culture sent.
A/P: Painless hematuria in a 67 y/o former heavy smoker - needs cystoscopy and upper tract imaging. Urgent urology referral today. Continue aspirin. Call if clots or can't urinate.

documents.title: Urine culture
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your urine culture showed no infection. That's why we still want urology to look - their office should call you this week. Let us know if you haven't heard by Thursday.

documents.title: Urology appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called urology to check on the urgent referral. Pt is booked 7/26, earliest they had. Asked them to call if a cancellation opens. Pt informed.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Seen 07/26/2023.

Re: Herbert Talbot, 67M. Referred for hematuria.
HPI: painless visible hematuria on and off for about two months. No dysuria, urgency or frequency.
PMH: HTN (well controlled), CHF, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis, treated TB, actinic keratosis, presbycusis.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Social: 40 pack-years, quit about ten years ago.
Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 78.
Exam: unremarkable.
Data: urinalysis with RBCs, no casts, no evidence of infection. CBC and chemistries normal.
Assessment: painless hematuria in a former heavy smoker; bladder neoplasm must be excluded.
Plan: CT urogram, then cystoscopy. Will be in touch with results.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT urogram, multiphase. Kidneys normal in size and enhancement, no renal mass, no hydronephrosis, no calculi. Collecting systems and ureters opacify normally without filling defect. Bladder: 3 cm enhancing mass along the right lateral wall. No pelvic adenopathy. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: 3 cm right lateral wall bladder mass, suspicious for urothelial neoplasm. Upper tracts normal.

documents.title: CT urogram reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT urogram copy received: 3 cm bladder wall mass. Called pt - urology has already told him and scheduled the scope with resection for 8/22. He's anxious but steady. Daughter will drive.

reports.text: Specimen: bladder tumor, right lateral wall, transurethral resection. Microscopic: papillary fronds lined by urothelium with mild architectural and cytologic atypia, low mitotic activity. No invasion of lamina propria. Detrusor muscle present in specimen and free of tumor. No lymphovascular invasion.
reports.conclusion: Low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma, noninvasive (pTa). Muscularis propria present, not involved.

procedures.procedure: Cystoscopy and transurethral resection of neoplasm of urinary bladder

documents.title: Cystoscopy and TURBT
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology, ambulatory surgery. Date of procedure 08/22/2023. Received 09/01/2023.
Procedure: cystoscopy, transurethral resection of bladder tumor.
Anesthesia: general. Findings: urethra normal, prostate mildly enlarged, single papillary tumor about 3 cm on the right lateral wall, well away from the ureteric orifice. No other lesions. Complete resection with deep bites including muscle. Hemostasis good. Single postoperative instillation of gemcitabine in recovery, held one hour, drained.
Allergies: NKDA.
Pathology (8/25): low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma, pTa, muscle present and uninvolved.
Plan: catheter out next morning (done). Surveillance cystoscopy at 3 months, then 9 months later, then yearly if clear.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks out from bladder tumor resection. Urine clear since the catheter came out. Some burning the first two days, gone.
Went over the path with him: low-grade, didn't invade, all removed; the risk is it comes back, which is why urology will scope him every few months at first. He wrote the schedule down. Reminded him smoking was the big risk factor and he did the right thing quitting.
BP and HF stable, no edema.
A/P: Bladder urothelial carcinoma pTa low grade s/p TURBT - surveillance per urology (first scope ~late Nov). Hematuria resolved. HTN/HFpEF unchanged. BMP.
Flu/COVID next month.

documents.title: Office Visit - cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter made the appointment. Dry cough for about 3 months that won't go away, and his pants are loose - down from 163 lb in May to 147 today. Appetite off. No fever, no night sweats, no blood in sputum. Breathing no worse than usual, no leg swelling.
Exam: thinner in the face. Breath sounds decreased over the right upper chest; otherwise clear. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: Persistent cough with 7+ kg weight loss in a 40 pack-year former smoker with prior TB - concerning for malignancy. CXR today in our imaging suite. Cancelled the old screening CT order; will go straight to diagnostic CT depending on film. Daughter aware.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison none available on plain film. Right upper lobe mass. Remaining lungs clear. No effusion. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contour normal.
reports.conclusion: Right upper lobe mass. CT chest recommended.

orders.reason: right upper lobe mass on CXR

documents.title: CXR result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt and daughter with CXR: mass in the right upper lung. Explained it needs a CT and likely a biopsy, that we can't call it cancer yet but have to treat it that seriously. CT chest with contrast ordered, scheduling for next week. They had good questions; daughter will come to everything.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Right upper lobe: 4.0 cm spiculated mass. No additional pulmonary nodules. No hilar or mediastinal lymph node enlargement. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Visualized adrenal glands, liver and bones without lesions.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm spiculated right upper lobe mass, highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. No evidence of metastatic disease.

documents.title: CT result and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT: 4 cm spiculated RUL mass, no spread seen on this scan. Spoke with pt and daughter. Urgent pulmonology referral sent; I called their office and they'll see him within 2 weeks. He asked straight out if it's cancer - told him most likely, and that no spread on CT is the best news we could have today.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit 08/06/2024. Received 08/08/2024.

Referral: RUL mass.
HPI: 69-year-old man, hypertension, heart failure, and low-grade bladder urothelial carcinoma resected in 2023, with three months of persistent cough and unexplained weight loss. No fever, sweats or hemoptysis. Pulmonary TB treated about 20 years ago.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81 (HCTZ per patient). NKDA.
Social: 40 pack-years, quit 2012.
Exam: cachectic appearance. Diminished breath sounds over the right upper lobe. No palpable lymphadenopathy.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7,500, plt 250,000, Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, Ca 10.2, alk phos 120, CEA 11.4 (elevated).
Imaging: CXR with RUL mass; CT 4 cm spiculated RUL mass without evidence of metastasis.
Impression: RUL mass, likely primary lung cancer.
Plan: PET-CT for staging, then CT-guided core biopsy. Will discuss at our thoracic conference once tissue is back.

reports.text: FDG PET-CT. Right upper lobe 4 cm spiculated mass, intensely FDG avid, SUVmax 9.6. No FDG-avid hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes. No abnormal uptake in liver, adrenals or skeleton. Physiologic activity elsewhere.
reports.conclusion: Hypermetabolic RUL mass consistent with primary lung malignancy. No nodal or distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: PET-CT reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: PET copy in: RUL mass avid, no nodes, nothing distant. Biopsy 8/20.

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe
conditions.note: adenocarcinoma, clinical stage IB (T2a N0 M0)

reports.text: Specimen: lung, right upper lobe, CT-guided core biopsy, 3 cores. Microscopic: infiltrating malignant glands with acinar architecture in a desmoplastic stroma. Immunohistochemistry: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma, consistent with lung primary.

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous core needle biopsy of lung

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Path received: lung adenocarcinoma. With PET, stage IB (T2a N0 M0). Pulmonology has told him; their conference is 9/3. Called him - he's okay, said he'd 'rather know.' Biopsy site fine, no shortness of breath after. Added to problem list.

documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Office cystoscopy 08/27/2024, received 08/29. History low-grade pTa urothelial carcinoma right lateral wall, TURBT 8/2023; last cystoscopy 11/2023 negative. Flexible cystoscopy: resection scar right lateral wall well healed. No papillary or flat lesions. Urethra normal. Impression: no evidence of recurrence. Next cystoscopy in 1 year. Aware of new lung diagnosis; no change to our plan.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 09/03/2024.
Diagnosis: RUL adenocarcinoma, cT2a N0 M0, stage IB.
Reviewed at multidisciplinary thoracic conference with thoracic surgery and radiation oncology. Given his heart failure and recent weight loss, the group favored stereotactic body radiotherapy over lobectomy. Discussed with patient and daughter today; he prefers SBRT. Referred to radiation oncology, simulation next week. Surveillance CT chest every 3-6 months afterward through radiation oncology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in to go over everything with me. Understands the cancer is early, hasn't spread, and that radiation was chosen because surgery would be hard on his heart. Simulation done, treatments start 9/23, five sessions. Cough the same, appetite a little better; weight 145 lb, holding.
Mood: worried but sleeping. PHQ-2 1.
Exam: decreased breath sounds R upper field, otherwise clear. No edema.
A/P: RUL adenocarcinoma stage IB - SBRT per rad onc. HFpEF/HTN stable. Encouraged calories, protein shakes fine. Bladder surveillance clear 8/27. Flu, COVID and RSV in October.

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
Outside radiation oncology. Treatment summary, received 10/08/2024.
Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma right upper lobe, cT2a N0 M0, stage IB.
Treatment: stereotactic body radiotherapy, 50 Gy in 5 fractions, 09/23/2024 to 10/03/2024, 4D-CT planning.
Tolerance: mild fatigue. No esophagitis. No change in breathing.
Follow-up: CT chest at 3 months, then every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. Allergies NKDA.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu, RSV and COVID given per PCP (RSV indicated with heart failure, age 69). Radiation finished 10/3, says he's just tired. Observed 15 min.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 3 months after SBRT. Comparison 7/24/2024. Treated RUL mass now 2.6 cm with surrounding post-treatment ground-glass change. No new nodules. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Treated RUL lesion decreased in size, now 2.6 cm, with expected post-radiation change. No new disease.

documents.title: Post-SBRT CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rad onc 3-month CT copy: mass shrinking, 2.6 cm, no new disease. Good.

events.reason: blood pressure and heart failure follow-up

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels better than in the summer. Cough much less, eating well, weight back up to 151 lb. Energy returning. No dyspnea beyond baseline, no edema.
Seen 3-month CT - lesion smaller.
Exam: lungs clear, no crackles. Neck veins flat, ankles without swelling.
A/P: Weight loss resolved with treatment. RUL adenocarcinoma s/p SBRT - rad onc surveillance. HTN/HFpEF stable, continue all meds. BMP. Cardiology follow-up next month (annual). RTC spring AWV.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Office visit 01/28/2025. Faxed 04/22/2025 at practice request.

Follow-up for HFpEF and hypertension. 69-year-old with hyperlipidemia and recently treated lung cancer (SBRT fall 2024).
New complaint: aching in both legs, building over two months. Constant and dull, worse with walking, better at rest. No injury.
Meds: metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20. NKDA.
Exam: skin normal over the legs, distal pulses palpable, no edema. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs; tender to palpation over the thigh and hip girdle muscles.
Labs: CK 600 (ref 38-174), AST 40, ALT 45, TSH 2.5, LDL 90.
Assessment: statin-associated muscle symptoms with mild CK elevation. Euvolemic HFpEF.
Plan: hold atorvastatin 4 weeks, repeat CK, then decide on rechallenge.

Addendum 02/25/2025: aches resolved off statin, CK 142. Restarted atorvastatin 40 mg daily as rechallenge; to call if aches return. Annual follow-up.

documents.title: heart doctor stopped my cholesterol pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The heart doctor said my leg aches might be from the atorvastatin and told me to stop it for a month and get a blood test after. Just so you know. Is that ok with you?

documents.title: RE: heart doctor stopped my cholesterol pill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. The doctor says that's a reasonable plan - follow cardiology's instructions and keep your other medicines the same. We'll ask their office to send us the visit note.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 6 months after SBRT. Comparison 12/10/2024. Treated RUL lesion now a 2.4 cm consolidative scar-like opacity with linear margins. No new nodules. No adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Evolving post-radiation change at the RUL treatment site. No evidence of recurrence or new disease.

documents.title: Surveillance CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 6-month CT reviewed: scar-like change 2.4 cm, nothing new.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request to cardiology for the January visit note and labs. They say it was 'not finalized' - will fax when signed.

conditions.label: Statin-associated muscle symptoms
conditions.note: CK 600 on atorvastatin 1/2025; resolved off drug, rechallenged 2/2025 without recurrence

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Cardiology note from January finally arrived last week: CK 600 with leg aches, statin held 4 wks, CK 142 and aches gone, restarted atorva 40 as rechallenge. He says legs fine since restarting. Added statin-associated muscle symptoms to the list.
Function: independent, walking most days. No falls. PHQ-2 0.
Lung ca: 6-month CT stable. Bladder: next scope September.
HTN/HFpEF: BP at goal, weight 152 lb, no edema.
Labs today. Colonoscopy due 2027.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request: lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, 90-day. Approved with 3 refills.

events.reason: worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Bilateral pleural effusions, layering. Post-treatment scarring right upper lobe, unchanged in character from prior CT. Heart size at upper limits of normal.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral pleural effusions.

reports.text: Specimen: pleural fluid, right, thoracentesis. Cytology: mesothelial cells, scattered lymphocytes and macrophages.
reports.conclusion: Negative for malignant cells.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, a regional hospital. Seen 08/04/2025; faxed to us 08/26/2025.

CC: shortness of breath.
HPI: 70M with heart failure, seen by his cardiologist this year, presenting with a week of progressive breathlessness, about 5 kg weight gain by home scale and worsening swelling of both legs. Lung adenocarcinoma treated with SBRT 2024. Bladder cancer resected 2023.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 22.
Exam: breath sounds reduced at both bases, no crackles. JVP elevated. Pitting edema both legs.
CXR: bilateral pleural effusions.
Given cancer history, diagnostic thoracentesis performed on the right: pleural protein 1.5 g/dL with serum protein 6.0 (ratio <0.5); pleural LDH 110 with serum LDH 200 (ratio <0.6). Transudate by Light's criteria. NT-proBNP 3,420.
Impression: acute decompensated heart failure with bilateral transudative effusions.
Disposition: IV furosemide given, admitted to medicine.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 08/04/2025, discharged 08/07/2025. Received 08/26/2025.
Principal diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure (preserved EF).
Course: diuresed with IV furosemide, net loss 4.5 kg. Breathing back to baseline on room air by day 2. Pleural cytology from the ED thoracentesis negative for malignant cells. Creatinine stable throughout.
Discharge weight 69.5 kg.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home - lisinopril 20 daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 daily, furosemide 40 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Instructions: weigh daily, call for gain of more than 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week; limit salt. Follow up with PCP within 1 week and cardiology within 1 month.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Daughter calling - admitted
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called: dad was admitted last night through the ER for fluid on the lungs and swelling, his heart failure. They drained fluid from one side. He's feeling better already. Expected home in a couple of days. Will book follow-up within a week of discharge. Asked hospital to fax records.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since 8/7 after 3 nights in for decompensated heart failure; ED drained fluid from the R chest, he was told it wasn't cancer. Discharge paperwork not here yet - history from pt and daughter and his discharge med sheet. Meds unchanged.
Now: breathing at baseline, sleeping flat, home weight 153 lb daily. Watching salt.
Exam: weight 69.5 kg. Lungs clear. JVP not elevated. Trace ankle edema.
A/P: ADHF, resolved, euvolemic now on home furosemide 40 daily. Daily weights - call for 2 lb/day or 5 lb/week. BMP today. Cardiology follow-up being scheduled by hospital. Will review summary when it arrives.

documents.title: Post-discharge weight check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt one week after his visit. Home weights 152.5-153.5 lb, no swelling, breathing fine, using less salt. Cardiology follow-up booked for September. Reinforced call parameters.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED and discharge summary from 8/4-8/7 reviewed. Transudate by Light's criteria, cytology negative, NT-proBNP 3,420. Discharged on home meds. Matches what we did 8/13.

documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Office cystoscopy 09/09/2025. Low-grade pTa urothelial carcinoma resected 8/2023, prior scopes clear. Bladder mucosa normal throughout; healed scar right lateral wall. No tumor. Next cystoscopy 1 year.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 12 months after SBRT. Comparison 3/11/2025. Right upper lobe post-radiation fibrosis, stable to slightly smaller. No new nodules. No adenopathy. Previously described pleural effusions resolved.
reports.conclusion: Stable post-radiation fibrosis. No recurrence.

documents.title: 12-month CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: One year out: stable fibrosis, no recurrence, effusions gone.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID given. Weight log reviewed - steady around 153. No reaction.

events.reason: transient loss of vision right eye

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 21 days

reports.text: Noncontrast head CT. No acute hemorrhage, mass effect or territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Orbits unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial abnormality.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Normal intervals. No acute ST changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm.

reports.text: Bilateral carotid duplex. Right internal carotid artery: heterogeneous plaque at the origin with velocities in the 50-69% stenosis range. Left internal carotid artery: no hemodynamically significant stenosis. Vertebral flow antegrade bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: Right ICA stenosis 50-69%. No significant left ICA stenosis.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, a regional hospital. Seen 12/01/2025; faxed 12/03/2025.

CC: vision loss right eye, resolved.
HPI: 70M with heart failure (admitted for decompensation in August), hypertension and hyperlipidemia. About 2 hours before arrival, sudden painless loss of vision in the right eye lasting roughly 10 minutes, then full recovery. No symptoms now. Very shaken by it.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Exam: visual acuity and fields grossly intact. Fundoscopic exam without abnormality. Neuro exam nonfocal.
CT head: no acute process. ECG: sinus rhythm. Carotid duplex: right ICA 50-69% stenosis, left without significant stenosis.
Impression: amaurosis fugax, right eye, with ipsilateral carotid stenosis.
Plan: continue aspirin, add clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 21 days. Continue statin. Vascular surgery referral. Return for any recurrence, weakness or speech change. Discharged home with daughter.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED 12/1 for 10 min of painless vision loss R eye. No repeat episodes. No weakness, numbness or speech trouble. Taking clopidogrel with aspirin, done around 12/22. No bleeding or bruising.
ED record reviewed: CT head neg, ECG sinus, duplex R ICA 50-69%.
Exam: neuro nonfocal. No carotid bruit appreciated. Lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: Amaurosis fugax from R carotid stenosis - resolved. Finish 21 days clopidogrel then aspirin alone. Vascular surgery referral sent today. Atorvastatin 40 continued. BP at goal. Reviewed stroke warning signs with him and daughter - call 911.

documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Outside vascular surgery group. Consult 01/13/2026. Sent 03/03/2026 after second request.

Reason: symptomatic right ICA stenosis.
History: 70-year-old man with a single 10-minute episode of right monocular vision loss on 12/1/2025, none since. Duplex at that visit: right ICA 50-69%, left without significant stenosis. HFpEF with admission 8/2025; lung adenocarcinoma treated with SBRT 2024; low-grade bladder cancer resected 2023. Former smoker, quit 2012.
Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40; clopidogrel course completed. NKDA.
Exam: alert, neurologically intact. No cervical bruit.
Assessment: symptomatic moderate right ICA stenosis.
Discussion: reviewed endarterectomy versus best medical therapy. Considering his heart failure, treated lung cancer and age, we and the patient chose medical management: aspirin, statin, blood pressure control.
Plan: repeat carotid duplex in 6 months; return sooner for any new symptoms.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt says he saw vascular surgery on the 13th and they decided 'no surgery for now.' Requested the consult note from their office.

documents.title: Vascular letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vascular note from January (requested twice). Medical management of R ICA 50-69%, repeat duplex July. No changes to his list.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 18 months after SBRT. Comparison 9/16/2025. Right upper lobe post-radiation fibrosis unchanged. No new pulmonary nodules. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable treatment-related fibrosis. No evidence of recurrence.

documents.title: 18-month CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rad onc surveillance CT: stable, no recurrence. Next in 6 months per their schedule.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check. Roomed 35 min late - the clinic was running behind after an add-on.
Usually easygoing and on time. Today short with the MA at intake, called the wait room 'a disaster.' When I came in he cut me off: said he's tired of waiting every single time and won't be treated like he doesn't matter. Arms crossed, not looking at me.
I acknowledged the wait was long and that his time matters, and apologized. Asked if anything else was going on - says no, just fed up. Settled after a few minutes and we went on.
Interval: no further vision episodes. No dyspnea beyond baseline, weights steady ~154. Legs fine on atorvastatin. No hematuria.
PHQ-2 1. Denies feeling down most days.
Exam: lungs clear, RRR, no edema. Neuro nonfocal.
A/P:
1. Situational irritability over the wait - addressed; no mood disorder suspected. Will check in next visit.
2. HTN/HFpEF - stable, continue all.
3. R ICA stenosis, medical management - repeat duplex July per vascular.
4. Lung adenoca s/p SBRT, bladder ca s/p TURBT - surveillance per specialists, both clear.
5. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
Front desk asked to book him first slot of the day next time. RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Talbot, your labs from yesterday are stable - kidneys, potassium, blood count all normal and cholesterol where it has been. No changes. Your July visit is booked for 8:00 am, first appointment of the day.

documents.title: Appointment reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Reminder call for 7/31 8:00 visit. Pt confirmed, also has the vascular ultrasound on 7/14. No concerns.

reports.text: Bilateral carotid duplex, 6-month follow-up. Comparison 12/1/2025. Right ICA: plaque at origin, velocities in the 50-69% range, unchanged. Left ICA: no hemodynamically significant stenosis. Vertebral arteries antegrade.
reports.conclusion: Stable right ICA stenosis 50-69%.

documents.title: Carotid duplex
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vascular's repeat duplex report received: R ICA 50-69% unchanged. Continue medical management.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First slot, roomed on time. He opened by apologizing for May - 'I was a bear that day.' No hard feelings; irritability resolved.
Feels well. Walking most mornings. Weights 153-155. No orthopnea, no swelling. No vision changes.
Carotid duplex 7/14 stable.
Exam: lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.
A/P: HTN/HFpEF stable - continue lisinopril, metoprolol, HCTZ, furosemide. Atorva 40 and ASA. BMP today. Urology scope in August, rad onc CT in September. RTC 3 months with flu shot.
